# taskmill

> taskmill runs background tasks for Go from your PostgreSQL database. Tasks commit with your data, run at least once, and survive a crashed worker.

The Go doc comments are the API reference: the comment of each identifier
states its default, its limits, and its errors. Run `go doc <package>` for the
map of a package, and `go doc <package>.<Name>` for one identifier. The pages
teach, and hold what has no identifier. Their paths start at the module's root.

## Packages

- `github.com/code19m/taskmill`: Package taskmill is a task queue and transactional outbox for Go, on PostgreSQL.
- `github.com/code19m/taskmill/outbox`: Package outbox publishes messages to a message broker reliably, with the transactional outbox pattern.
- `github.com/code19m/taskmill/ui`: Package ui serves taskmill's dashboard as an HTTP handler.
- `github.com/code19m/taskmill/cmd/taskmill-ui`: Command taskmill-ui serves taskmill's dashboard as a program of its own, apart from the applications that use the installation.
- `github.com/code19m/taskmill/taskmilltest`: Package taskmilltest helps test code that uses taskmill.
- `github.com/code19m/taskmill/otel`: Package otel instruments taskmill with OpenTelemetry traces and metrics, following OpenTelemetry's semantic conventions for messaging.

- [Why taskmill](docs/start/why-taskmill.md): you want to know if taskmill fits your project, and what it does not do
- [Fit taskmill to your architecture](docs/start/architectures.md): you want to know where taskmill's parts go in a monolith, modules, services, serverless functions, several regions, or an app with tenants
- [Quickstart](docs/start/quickstart.md): you want to run your first task and see it in the dashboard, in about 15 minutes

## Guides

- [Set up the database and client](docs/guides/setup.md): Create taskmill's tables, and connect to them
- [Define tasks](docs/guides/define-tasks.md): Write a task type, and choose what goes in it
- [Enqueue tasks](docs/guides/enqueue.md): Run a task now, later, or before others
- [Use your own transactions](docs/guides/transactions.md): Send an email only if the order was saved
- [Handle tasks](docs/guides/handle-tasks.md): Write the code that does the work
- [Retries and errors](docs/guides/retries-and-errors.md): Know how often a failing task is retried, and what a dead task is
- [Handle tasks in batches](docs/guides/batch-handlers.md): Do work that is cheaper in bulk, such as a bulk insert
- [Add middleware](docs/guides/middleware.md): Run your own code around every task: metrics, a log line, a tenant
- [Workers and queues](docs/guides/workers-and-queues.md): Run workers, limit how many tasks run, or pause a queue
- [Task order and FIFO groups](docs/guides/ordering.md): Run one account's tasks one at a time, in order
- [Avoid duplicate tasks](docs/guides/deduplication.md): Never enqueue the same task twice
- [Run tasks on a schedule](docs/guides/schedules.md): Run a report every night at 03:00
- [Publish events with the outbox](docs/guides/outbox.md): Publish events to Kafka, NATS, or RabbitMQ only after a commit
- [The dashboard](docs/guides/dashboard.md): See and fix tasks in a browser
- [Manage tasks from code](docs/guides/operations-api.md): Retry, cancel, or delete thousands of tasks from code
- [Logs, traces, and metrics](docs/guides/observability.md): Get logs, traces, metrics, and queue depth
- [Test your code](docs/guides/testing.md): Test code that enqueues and handles tasks

## How do I…?

- [Do work once](docs/recipes/do-work-once.md): Charge a card once, although a task may run twice. An idempotency key from the task ID, and `Task.CompleteTx` for your own data
- [Call a rate-limited API](docs/recipes/call-a-rate-limited-api.md): Respect a partner's limit: 4 calls at the same time, or 600 a minute. Its own queue with `MaxRunning`, one row that spaces the calls, and `Snooze` on HTTP 429
- [Keep order per key](docs/recipes/keep-order-per-key.md): Apply one account's events in order. A `GroupKey` per account
- [Share a queue fairly between customers or tenants](docs/recipes/share-a-queue-between-customers.md): Stop one customer's big batch from delaying all the others, or serve many tenants. A queue for batch work, a `GroupKey` per customer, and one schema for all tenants
- [Keep at most one waiting task per key](docs/recipes/one-waiting-task-per-key.md): Run one refresh for 50 changes to the same product. A flag in your own row, set in the transaction that enqueues
- [Cancel or replace a delayed task](docs/recipes/cancel-a-delayed-task.md): Stop a reminder when the customer pays, or move it to another day. `CancelTx` in the transaction that changes your data, and a check in the handler
- [Run a task at each customer's local time](docs/recipes/run-at-each-customers-local-time.md): Send each customer a summary at 09:00 local time. A due time per customer in your own table, and one schedule that enqueues what is due
- [Move a cron job to a schedule](docs/recipes/move-a-cron-job-to-a-schedule.md): Replace a crontab line. A `Schedule` with the same five fields, and a `Location`
- [Consume from a broker](docs/recipes/consume-from-a-broker.md): Act on Kafka messages without doing the work twice. Enqueue with the message ID as `DedupeKey`
- [Change a task safely](docs/recipes/change-a-task-safely.md): Change a payload, rename a kind, or move it to another queue. A new kind, in three deploys
- [Run long tasks](docs/recipes/run-long-tasks.md): Run tasks that take 10 minutes or more. A longer `Timeout` and `DrainTimeout`. Split work that takes hours
- [Recover from an incident](docs/recipes/recover-from-an-incident.md): Retry 5,000 dead tasks after a fix. Pause the queue, `RetryMatching`, then resume
- [Organize tasks by module](docs/recipes/organize-tasks-by-module.md): Keep each module's tasks apart in one binary. A package of task types and a queue per module, and one schema
- [Split work across services](docs/recipes/split-across-services.md): Run several services, or give work to another one. One schema per service, and a `Client` for the other's schema
- [Work with other languages](docs/recipes/work-with-other-languages.md): Start a Go service's task from Node.js, Python, or another language. An HTTP endpoint that enqueues, with a map of the allowed kinds
- [One dashboard for many services](docs/recipes/one-dashboard-for-many-services.md): See every service in one admin app. A dashboard in each service. The admin app forwards a path to each
- [Use your own migration tool](docs/recipes/use-your-migration-tool.md): Use goose, Atlas, or Flyway. Apply `taskmill.Migrations` with your tool

- [Production checklist](docs/production/checklist.md): you prepare to go live

- [Deploys](docs/production/deploys.md): you ship a new version of your app, change a task, or run on a serverless platform
- [Kubernetes](docs/production/kubernetes.md): you want manifests to copy
- [Autoscaling](docs/production/autoscaling.md): you want KEDA to add and remove workers

- [Security](docs/production/security.md): you protect the dashboard, the database, and the data in your tasks
- [Troubleshooting](docs/production/troubleshooting.md): something is wrong right now
- [Upgrading](docs/production/upgrading.md): a new taskmill release is out

## How taskmill is built

- [Task lifecycle and guarantees](docs/design/task-lifecycle.md): The contract: every state change, the invariants, and how each guarantee is kept
- [Storage schema](docs/design/schema.md): The tables and indexes, and the reasoning behind them
- [Key statements](docs/design/schema-statements.md): The statements that enqueue, fetch, and complete tasks, and record their failures
- [Lists and counts](docs/design/schema-lists.md): The statements that list and count tasks, and why dead and canceled tasks come by finish time
- [Lists by creation time](docs/design/schema-creation-order.md): Why a list with a range of creation times has an order and two indexes of its own, and what they cost
- [Operator actions](docs/design/schema-operations.md): The statements that retry, cancel, and delete tasks, one or many
- [FIFO groups and deduplication](docs/design/schema-groups.md): How a group keeps its order, and how a dedupe key admits one task
- [Maintenance and notifications](docs/design/schema-maintenance.md): What the maintainer runs, and how workers are woken
- [Queue statistics and health](docs/design/schema-statistics.md): How the maintainer counts the queues, what lag leaves out, and what probes and autoscalers read
- [Rows that taskmill did not write](docs/design/schema-rows.md): Which values the tables refuse, and how the code survives the others
- [The API's shape](docs/design/api-shape.md): Why each point of the API has its shape, and when we look at it again
- [Dependencies and modules](docs/design/dependencies.md): Why pgx is the only dependency, why OpenTelemetry, the ORM examples, and the browser tests have modules of their own, and how to add a dependency
- [Benchmarks](docs/design/benchmarks.md): The performance targets, how we measure them, and the latest results
- [Releasing](docs/design/releasing.md): How the project team publishes a version
- [Writing docs](docs/design/writing-docs.md): The style guide and the page templates
- [Writing doc comments](docs/design/writing-godoc.md): What a doc comment holds, and how godoc and the pages share the work
